title: A state insurance regulator makes complaint recovery and market-availability work visible without closing the household outcome chain
source_unit: New York State Department of Financial Services Consumer Assistance Unit 2025 annual report and property-insurance data-call instructions
geography: New York State regulatory and consumer-assistance system; national referrals can occur in the complaint workflow

observations.period: Calendar 2025; DFS insurance complaint and recovery workflow

denominator.unit: insurance complaints received by the Consumer Assistance Unit

observations.method: DFS Consumer Assistance Unit annual administrative report; counts describe routed complaints, closures, referrals, inquiries, and reported recovery, not a probability sample of all insurance problems.
observations.uncertainty: Receipt and closure counts may include multiple contacts or cases, and recovery totals do not measure total loss, claim adequacy, time to payment, or whether a consumer regarded the result as sufficient.
observations.subgroup: New York insurance complainants and inquiries handled by DFS, with cases categorized by insurance type and other administrative classifications.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large recovery total can reflect successful intervention, large individual cases, provider settlements, or accounting conventions; complaint volume can reflect awareness and access to DFS rather than market-wide prevalence.

denominator.unit: property-casualty and service-contract complaints closed by DFS

positive_outcome_share.unit: percent of closed property-casualty and service-contract complaints

observations.method: DFS annual complaint table for the property-casualty and service-contract category; positive consumer outcome is the agency's reported administrative label.
observations.uncertainty: The category combines property-casualty insurance and service contracts; the report does not provide a household-level denominator, severity distribution, time-to-resolution, claim type, or outcome adequacy measure.
observations.subgroup: Closed New York property-casualty and service-contract complaint cases handled by DFS.
observations.counterinterpretation: A positive-outcome label is not the same as full claim payment, coverage restoration, repair completion, or prevention of future harm; complainants who never reach DFS are outside the denominator.

observations.period: 2025 annual availability survey; homeowners-insurance market governance for 2026

denominator.unit: New York DFS statutory data-call and homeowners-insurance supplement

homeowners_supplement.value: underwriting plans for homeowners insurance in 2026, with attention to areas of catastrophic-loss exposure

observations.method: DFS data-call letter under New York Insurance Law section 308; an institutional reporting requirement, not a published estimate of availability or affordability.
observations.uncertainty: The data-call mechanism shows what the regulator is requesting and monitoring; the reviewed letter does not itself supply the insurer responses or a market-wide availability estimate.
observations.subgroup: Licensed insurers writing homeowners insurance in New York, with special attention to high-catastrophe-exposure areas.
observations.counterinterpretation: A required survey can improve regulatory visibility without changing insurer behavior, consumer price, coverage, or claim outcomes.

reported_fields.value: policies canceled, nonrenewed, and other homeowners-policy terminations

reporting_scope.value: licensed property/casualty insurers meeting the stated direct-written-premium threshold

observations.method: DFS Regulation 154 quarterly reporting instructions for homeowners policies.
observations.uncertainty: The instructions document a data pipeline and reporting scope; they do not establish the number of cancellations, nonrenewals, reasons, affected households, replacement coverage, or subsequent mobility.
observations.subgroup: New York licensed property/casualty insurers and their homeowners-policy portfolios within the regulation's reporting threshold.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reporting requirements can improve measurement without implying that nonrenewal is increasing or that a policy termination was unjustified.

related_sources.claim: CBO supplies national disaster-loss and federal mortgage-exposure context for the regulator's state-level insurance route.
FHFA supplies an asset-price clock that should remain separate from complaint recovery and policy availability.
CFPB supplies a federal complaint-routing comparator with a different product scope, geography, taxonomy, and remedy boundary.

boundary: This record adds a state-regulatory visibility and recourse layer. It measures complaints, closures, agency labels, reported recoveries, and insurer-reporting requirements. It does not establish insurance-market prevalence, household claim adequacy, repair completion, premium affordability, nonrenewal causation, or political meaning.
